Audit v2 · VehicleControlAlgorithms · 3 Nov 2026

VehicleControlAlgorithms Audit v2

Superseded by v3. The same audit as v1 (removed; its findings are listed below), re-run on the updated code base. This round bounded every tunable parameter (with a physics-based speed cap under the Dynamic model), validated JSON inputs, regenerated the infeasible map_02 path, and reduced CPU and memory use. Every build, smoke, unit and closed-loop stage was repeated and compared with v1.

Baseline scenario matrix69 / 72 v1 47Kinematic 35/36 (v1 35) · Dynamic 34/36 (v1 12)

GUI idle CPU0.2 % v1 3.0 %of one core; LQR tick 70 → 4 µs; MPPI 260 → 0 heap allocations per tick
Issues4 fixed · 7 mitigated19 still open of 30 (B30 found and fixed in this round)
  • Slider limitsOne table, include/tuning_limits.hpp, drives every slider and the JSON clamping. Max Delta stops at the vehicle’s tire angle. Under Dynamic, Max Speed stops at the path’s cap from path_tracking::AnalyzePathFeasibility. See Limits.
  • JSON clampingOut-of-range algorithm values are clamped at Start, and again when switching to Dynamic, with an on-screen list of what changed. VehicleLoader range-checks every field and reports it.
  • map_02 pathRegenerated by tools/generate_map02_path.py: 13-unit arcs with clothoid transitions, tightest bend 9.4 m (car) / 13.3 m (bus), ≥ 3.3 units body clearance to every baffle.
  • PerformanceEvent-driven idle rendering, LQR warm start, allocation-free MPC/MPPI, bounded debug log and trace, cached path plot, a live performance row in Simulation Info.
  • .gitignorebuild/, debug_logs/, imgui.ini, CMake/IDE output, harness binaries. data/ stays tracked.
  • DocsREADME, pipeline.md, pure_pursuit.md and lqr.md updated for the new ranges, map units, map_02 and render cadence.

Bug list with status

30 issues
▲ High● OpenB01Controller · LQREffort S

LQR curvature feed-forward is unsigned — it always steers left

src/path_tracking/lqr/lqr.cpp:183

Evidence
Unit test LQR-1b: on-path, aligned on a right-hand arc the output is +0.129 rad (left); expected −0.129 rad.
Root cause
ComputeCurvature() takes std::abs() of the cross product, so δ_ff = atan(L·κ) is positive on every bend. docs/lqr.md describes a signed Menger feed-forward. Adaptive PP shares the helper (adaptive_pure_pursuit.cpp:71) but only needs |κ|, so it is correct there.
Impact
On every right-hand bend the feed-forward pushes the wrong way and the feedback term has to overpower it, so LQR runs wide on right turns.
Proposal
Return the signed cross product (keep std::abs only in Adaptive PP). Add a left/right arc unit test.
▲ High● OpenB02Controller · MPCEffort M

MPC optimiser is bang-bang and numerically ill-conditioned

src/path_tracking/mpc/mpc.cpp:112-131

Status now
Still flips pass/fail under a 1 µm start offset in 2/6 Kinematic scenarios.
Evidence
Kinematic runs: median 16 steering sign flips/s and 30% of ticks at full lock. map_02/Car/Kinematic wandered 464 m off the path. A 1 µm change of the start position flips pass/fail in 2 of 6 scenarios (max-CTE spread 462 m).
Root cause
The gradient-descent step u -= lr·∇J has no scaling, line search or trust region. ∇J reaches about 10, so one 0.08-rate step moves a control by ~0.8 rad and it lands on ±max_delta. There is no Δδ (smoothness) cost, and the gradient is zero wherever the rollout rate limit masks a control.
Impact
Erratic, actuator-hostile commands. Results are not reproducible across builds or tiny input changes.
Proposal
Cap the per-iteration step (prototype: ±0.05 rad), add a w_rate·(Δδ)² term on the rate-limited sequence, and optimise in Δδ space or use a QP (OSQP/qpOASES) or iLQR. Prototype result on Kinematic: max CTE 2.6 → 0.4–0.8 m, time at lock 29% → 0%.
▲ High● OpenB03Controller · MPCEffort S

MPC rollout is anchored to its last command, not the real wheel angle

src/path_tracking/mpc/mpc.cpp:119, 121, 133, 135

Evidence
Unit test MPC-2: the first command is 0.563 rad when only 0.0225 rad is reachable in one rollout step (the actuator needs 2.5 s). The user’s CSV from 2026-07-21 19:24 shows ±32° bang-bang commands while the applied angle lags far behind.
Root cause
last_output_ = u_[0] is the unconstrained command. The rollout assumes the wheel already sits there, so it predicts manoeuvres the rate-limited actuator cannot follow. IPathTrackingAlgorithm only receives VehicleState, which has no actuator state.
Impact
This is the “round-3 fix” from IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS. It did not resolve the map_03 spin-out: the CSV still ends inside the top-left obstacle after 56.8 s.
Proposal
Add an applied steering_angle field to VehicleState, filled by both vehicle models, and anchor the rollout on it. On its own this is not enough (see B02); ship the two together.
▲ High● OpenB04Simulation loopEffort S

Goal test is a hard 1 m radius with no end-of-path handling, so runs never terminate

src/vehicle_control_ui.cpp:638

Status now
Fewer near-misses now that Dynamic speed is capped, but the goal test is unchanged.
Evidence
9 of 22 failed baseline runs passed the goal 1.2–3.9 m away and then drove off the map forever. Example: Adaptive PP/Bus/Dynamic on map_01 never collides, misses by 1.92 m and keeps running.
Root cause
Only the rear axle within 1 m of the goal counts. After the last waypoint every tracker keeps chasing path.back(), and there is no timeout or failure state.
Impact
The simulation hangs in RUNNING; the debug log grows without bound (B22); the result is reported as a failure.
Proposal
Finish when the vehicle crosses the goal plane on the last segment with |CTE| below a tolerance (prototype: 3 m), or when progress reaches 100%. Add SIM_FAILED with a timeout and an off-map/collision check. Make the radius configurable per map.
▲ High◐ MitigatedB05Data · vehicle + mapsEffort M

Dynamic fidelity fails because a slow steering actuator meets paths with curvature jumps

data/vehicle/vehicle0{1,2}.json (max_steering_wheel_rate); data/maps/map_0{1,3}/path.json

Status now
Dynamic Max Speed is now capped per path from steering rate, friction and curvature; map_02 has clothoid transitions. map_01/03 still use line-arc fillets (curvature steps), so their caps are low (1.4–2.1 m/s).
Evidence
Same code, same maps: Kinematic 35/36 clean, Dynamic 12/36. Dynamic with the rate limit off: 35/36. With a 600 °/s EPS rate: 26/36. At 2 m/s Dynamic passes 29/36; at 12 m/s, 2/36.
Root cause
200 °/s (car) and 250 °/s (bus) at the wheel are only 12.9 °/s and 15.6 °/s at the road wheel. The map_01/03 paths were filleted with line + arc segments, so curvature steps from 0 to 1/R instantly, which needs an infinite steering rate. KinematicBicycleModel has no actuator at all, so it hides the problem.
Impact
Every controller overshoots fillet entries under Dynamic fidelity. Only MPC is (partly) rate-aware.
Proposal
(1) Re-smooth the paths with clothoid / G2 transitions. (2) Plan speed from curvature and its rate: v ≤ δ̇_max / (L·dκ/ds). (3) Check the EPS rate against data (500–700 °/s is typical). (4) Use the same steering actuator model in both fidelities so Kinematic is a fair baseline.
▲ High✓ FixedB06Data · map_02Effort S

The map_02 reference path is tighter than either vehicle can turn

data/maps/map_02/path.json

Status now
map_02 regenerated: tightest radius 9.4 m (Car 01) / 13.3 m (Bus 01), ≥3.3 units body clearance, tools/generate_map02_path.py checked in.
Evidence
In real metres the tightest bend is R = 2.34 m for Car 01 (needs 48° of road-wheel angle; maximum is 32.3°) and 3.30 m for Bus 01 (52.7° of 56.2°). All 12 Dynamic runs on map_02 fail.
Root cause
The path was authored in map units, and map units turn into metres through a vehicle-dependent scale (B10). IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS calls this path “already smooth throughout”, but it was never checked against the turning radius.
Impact
Infeasible for the car under any model; Kinematic passes only because the over-tight sections are short.
Proposal
Regenerate with R_min ≥ 1.5 × the largest vehicle turning radius, in metres. Add a CI check of path curvature against MaxTireAngle for each vehicle.
▲ High● OpenB07Vehicle model · ComposedEffort S

The Dynamic model integrates the CoG, but the UI and trackers treat (x, y) as the rear axle

src/vehicle/composed_vehicle_model.cpp:75-76

Status now
Still visible: Stanley + Bus 01 on map_02 fails above 2 m/s under Dynamic.
Evidence
Unit test VM-3: at 3 m/s in a steady turn, (x, y) moves 4.5° off the heading (CoG sideslip ≈ b/R). Kinematic gives 0°.
Root cause
Slip angles use CoG velocities (vx, vy), and the position is integrated with that same vy. The rear axle’s lateral velocity is vy − b·r. The UI draws (x, y) as the rear axle (DrawVehicle), Pure Pursuit uses it as the rear axle, and Stanley adds L·heading to it to get the front axle.
Impact
The body is drawn 1.5 m (car) or 2.3 m (bus) out of place and appears to crab in every bend. Stanley’s front-axle point is off by b. A fidelity switch silently moves the reference point.
Proposal
Integrate the rear axle: ẋ = vx·cosψ − (vy − b·r)·sinψ (2 lines). Note: the prototype shows LQR and Adaptive PP get WORSE under Dynamic with this fix (3/6 → 0/6), because the CoG offset was hiding their missing actuator model. Land it together with B05/B09/B17 actuator-aware control.
▲ High✓ FixedB08Controller · MPC / MPPIEffort S

Segmentation fault when horizon_N or horizon_T is 0

src/path_tracking/mpc/mpc.cpp:92, src/path_tracking/mppi/mppi.cpp:84

Status now
Horizon guards in Mpc/Mppi plus range clamping of every config value; both crash probes now return 0.
Evidence
Crash probes mpc_h0 and mppi_t0: ASan reports SEGV in std::swap; the release build exits with 139.
Root cause
std::rotate(u_.begin(), u_.begin()+1, u_.end()) and u_.back() run on an empty vector. The sliders stop at 5, but the JSON value is never validated.
Impact
A typo in config/path_tracking/mpc.json or mppi.json crashes the app on the first tick.
Proposal
Validate all loader values (B16); guard empty horizons.
◆ Medium● OpenB09Controller · MPPIEffort S

MPPI rolls out at max_speed·0.5, not the real speed, and ignores actuator limits

src/path_tracking/mppi/mppi.cpp:47

Status now
lambda floor added (no NaN); rollout speed and actuator model still wrong.
Evidence
Unit test MPPI-1: the output is identical at 0.5 m/s and 12 m/s. Dynamic: 0/6 per algorithm slice on the shipped code. The prototype (real speed + rate-limited rollout anchored on the applied angle) lifts MPPI Dynamic across all experiments from 12% to 63%.
Root cause
MPC had the same bug, and it was fixed only in MPC. MPPI has no rate limit, no control cost and no smoothing.
Impact
Wrong predictions at every speed other than half of max_speed. Under Kinematic, a median 21 sign flips/s of steering chatter.
Proposal
Use state.speed; add the rate limit and anchor (as for MPC); add a control or Δu cost and a Savitzky-Golay filter on u.
◆ Medium● OpenB10Simulation loopEffort M

The physical size of a map depends on the selected vehicle

src/vehicle_control_ui.cpp:364

Status now
Now documented in README; maps are still in vehicle-scaled units.
Evidence
simScale = vehicle_radius / real_half_width, so the 120 × 120-unit maps are 87.5 m wide for Car 01 and 123.5 m for Bus 01. The 12-unit fillets are 8.75 m for the car and 12.3 m for the bus.
Root cause
The map file sets vehicle_radius = 1.2 map units, and the sim rescales the world so the vehicle’s half-width equals it.
Impact
The same map is a different test for each vehicle; the 1 m goal tolerance and obstacle clearances change with it. README says “120 m × 120 m”.
Proposal
Author maps in metres (scale = 1). Use vehicle_radius only as an inflation radius for planning and clearance checks.
◆ Medium● OpenB11Vehicle model · ComposedEffort S

Explicit Euler on the tire dynamics is inaccurate or unstable at low speed and frame-rate dt

src/vehicle/composed_vehicle_model.cpp:60-78

Status now
Dynamic at 10 fps: 18/36 clean.
Evidence
Unit test VM-4, yaw-rate error against a 1 ms reference: 342% (0.6 m/s, 60 fps), 719% (0.6 m/s, 30 fps), 401% (1.0 m/s, 30 fps). The 10 fps sweep drops Kinematic to 30/36.
Root cause
The lateral eigenvalue is about (Cf+Cr)/(m·vx), roughly 176 s⁻¹ for the car at 0.5 m/s. Euler is stable only for dt < 2/λ ≈ 11 ms, and the sim steps at wall-clock dt of up to 100 ms.
Impact
Limit cycling and saturated-tire chatter just after the 0.5 m/s handover and on slow machines.
Proposal
Use a fixed-step accumulator (for example 1 kHz physics, 60 Hz render) or internal sub-stepping (prototype: 2 ms), or a semi-implicit / RK4 integrator.
◆ Medium● OpenB12Vehicle model · ComposedEffort S

The steering rate limit is bypassed below 0.5 m/s, and the wheel angle jumps at the handover

src/vehicle/composed_vehicle_model.cpp:102-103

Evidence
Unit test VM-1: 0.5 rad applied in one 16.7 ms step when the limit is 0.0038 rad. VM-2: the effective angle is 0.300 rad in the fallback and 0.0038 rad on the first dynamic step.
Root cause
KinematicFallback() is called before UpdateSteering(), and applied_steering_ is not updated while in the fallback.
Impact
At launch the car turns its wheels instantly, then they snap back to about 0° once it reaches 0.5 m/s.
Proposal
Run the steering subsystem first, unconditionally, and feed the applied angle into the fallback.

src/vehicle_control_ui.cpp:622

RebuildAlgorithm() calls make_unique plus SetPath(), which sets current_path_idx_ = 0 and clears LQR prev errors and the MPC/MPPI u_.

src/vehicle_control_ui.cpp:535, 611

Root cause
Model state is not carried over; there are two sources of truth for the vehicle data (vehicle_loader_ and simEffectiveVehicleData_).

◆ Medium◐ MitigatedB15LoadersEffort M

Vehicle and map loaders accept incomplete or truncated JSON without complaint

src/vehicle/vehicle_loader.cpp:126-188, src/map/map_loader.cpp:442-492

Status now
VehicleLoader range-checks every field, clamps and lists changes in a notification; failed loads now clear the selection. Map/path files are still not validated (LD-4).
Evidence
LD-1: a missing steering_wheel_to_tire_angle_ratio loads as 0, so MaxTireAngle = inf and steering is never clamped. LD-2: truncated vehicle JSON gives Load() = true. LD-3: the resulting model returns NaN yaw rate. LD-4: a truncated path.json invents the waypoint (40, 0).
Root cause
root.at(k) returns a zero JVal for missing keys and the 20-field block overwrites unconditionally (flagged in IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS but never fixed). The parser never reports a syntax error. The UI also keeps vehicleSelected/pathSelected = true after a failed reload, with zeroed data.
Impact
Silent NaN, inf or garbage simulations from one malformed file.
Proposal
Make keys required, check ranges, and return an error string that the UI shows. Consider a vetted single-header JSON library (nlohmann/json) instead of two copy-pasted parsers.

◆ Medium● OpenB17Controller · LQREffort M

LQR derivative states use a fixed time_step, and the first tick kicks

src/path_tracking/lqr/lqr.cpp:203-204, 124-125

Status now
DARE is now warm-started (70 → 3–4 µs), derivative handling unchanged.
Evidence
LQR-2: same pose twice gives −0.398 rad, then −0.199 rad. At 30 fps the error rates are overestimated 2.1× (Δe / 0.016 over a 0.033 s frame).
Root cause
prev errors start at 0 and the derivative divides by config time_step instead of the real frame dt. The model also has no steering-actuator state (B07).
Impact
Frame-rate-dependent gains; a kick after every Start or rebuild.
Proposal
Pass the real dt (or estimate rates from state: v·sin(e_ψ) and r − v·κ); seed prev on the first call; augment the model with δ as a state and δ̇ as the input.
◆ Medium◐ MitigatedB18Simulation loopEffort S

The speed controller has no acceleration, jerk or curvature limits

src/vehicle_control_ui.cpp:648

Status now

Evidence
a = 1.0·(v_max − v) gives 12 m/s² (1.22 g) at launch for Max Speed 12 m/s, applied identically to the 8.3 t bus. Speed sweep: Dynamic clean rate drops from 81% at 2 m/s to 6% at 12 m/s.
Root cause
A pure P term with gain 1; target speed constant along the whole path.
Impact
Unrealistic launches and braking; the controllers are tested at speeds the bends cannot support.

Clamp to vehicle-specific a_max/a_min (add to the vehicle JSON); compute a curvature-based speed profile (v ≤ √(a_lat,max/κ)); add a jerk limit.

Next steps

  1. B04: end-of-path goal test, timeout and failure state.
  2. Smooth map_01 and map_03 with the map_02 generator approach; their Dynamic caps rise from 1.4–2.1 m/s accordingly.
  3. B11 + B21: fixed-step physics (e.g. 1 kHz) decoupled from the frame rate; this also fixes the 10–15 fps Dynamic results.
  4. B07 with B17: rear-axle reference point together with an actuator-aware LQR (and Adaptive PP), never one without the other.
  5. B02/B03 MPC rewrite and B09 MPPI rollout fixes; B01 signed LQR curvature.
  6. B18: vehicle-specific acceleration/jerk limits; B13: update configs in place so live tuning keeps controller state.
  7. Run git rm --cached imgui.ini, commit the work on a branch, and add CI that runs ctest and this harness.

Manual GUI check

The GUI was launched, not driven. These steps confirm the new behaviour by hand:

  1. Car 01 · any algorithm · Sine Wave Map → Start: the reference path is the new arc-and-straight weave.
  2. Set Model to Dynamic (Linear Tire) and Start: a “Parameters limited” notification lists Max Speed 5 -> 2.43; the line “Max Speed limited to 2.4 m/s on this map (Dynamic)” sits under Override Defaults.
  3. Tick Override Defaults: Max Speed cannot be dragged past the cap; Max Delta (Stanley/MPC/MPPI) stops at 0.56 rad for Car 01 and 0.98 rad for Bus 01.
  4. Run under Kinematic at 5 m/s, then switch to Dynamic mid-run: speed drops to the cap and the notification appears; the right panel layout does not move.
  5. The Perf row shows about 60 fps and a tick time well under 1 ms while running (MPC ≈ 0.3 ms), and a few fps when idle; memory stays around 50 MB.
  6. Delete "wheelbase" from a copy of a vehicle JSON and select it: a “Vehicle file adjusted” notification names the field and the value used.
